page: Amazon Web Services m6id.32xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the Intel Xeon 8375C processor. It features 128 vCPUs and 64 physical cores with hyper-threading running at 3.5 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 512 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. It includes 7,600 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark results show strong multi-core capabilities, with the Passmark CPU score and CPU encryption test reaching the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance under stress-ng and memory bandwidth both rank in the top 25%. Single-core performance, including Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core tests, falls into the average category. The server demonstrates high efficiency in database operations, with Redis SET operations achieving 106.58 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaching 72.01 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m6id.32xlarge offers high resource density, combining substantial compute power with a massive 7.6 TB local NVMe SSD storage allocation. This bundled local storage reduces the need for external block storage for high-throughput workloads, though the volatile nature of instance store volumes represents a tradeoff that requires application-level replication. The server lacks GPU acceleration, making it less suitable for heavy deep learning training, though it maintains strong prompt processing speeds for smaller LLM inference workloads.

This configuration is highly suited for large-scale databases, high-throughput web serving, software compilation, and data-intensive applications that require fast local scratch space. It is also well-suited for containerized microservices, caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring balanced compute, memory, and high-speed local storage.
